capitals.name: Sozaq
capitals.note: Infobox 'Sozaq (c. 1465-1469)'; coordinates approximate to some 50 km (the site is in the Suzak district of the Turkistan region); the gazetteer has no Sozak. The site lies some 35 km outside Cliopatria's 1468 core; the 1465-1474 keyframes and the founding event add a 50 km disk round it.

capitals.name: Syghanaq (Sygnak, Sunaq Ata)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Syghanaq (1469-1511)', on the middle Syr Darya (Qyzylorda region); coordinates approximate to some 30 km; the gazetteer has no Sygnak. Abu'l-Khayr's capital from 1446 was Sighnaq (Abu'l-Khayr Khan page). The seat is kept here to 1519, not 1510, because the same page dates Kasym's capture of the Nogai capital Saray-Juk to 1520 (see Saraishyq); the Janibek Khan page has Janibek die about 1480 at 'Sighnaq, Kazakh Khanate'.

capitals.name: Saraishyq
capitals.note: Infobox 'Saraishyq (1511-1521)'; the dossier starts the seat in 1520, the year the Kazakh Khanate page has Kasym capture the Nogai capital Saray-Juk (the page does not say Saraishyq and Saray-Juk are one place; the Kasym Khan page has Kasym die at Saray-Juk), because Cliopatria keeps the lower Ural Nogai in every shape of 1519-1523 and the nogai-horde dossier keeps Saray-Jük (Saraichik) as the Nogai seat to 1577. Coordinates are the modern site of Saraishyq/Saraychik on the lower Ural, approximate to some 20 km (the gazetteer has none). The dot lies inside the 1520 contest zone (ledger 1520), not in a Kazakh keyframe.

capitals.name: Turkistan

The steppe is drawn from 1468, Cliopatria's first Kazakh year and the year the Sibir dossier loses it at Abu'l-Khayr's death (ledger 1468, confidence 1: the page's 'around 1470' is two years later). keyframe_review.note: 1475-1481, 739,787 km2 on Cliopatria, whose +1,925 cells of 1475 all come out of the Timurid shape (60.5-71.6E, 37.1-46.6N: Tashkent, Samarkand, Bukhara, Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, Khatlon). No page opened gives the Kazakhs any of these: the Moghulistan page has Yunus Khan take Tashkent from the Timurids ('In 1484 he captured Tashkent from the Timurids'; 1482 in another place), and the Muhammad Shaybani page has him oust 'the Timurids from their capital Samarkand in 1500'. Remove Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan; the rest of the shape (Syr Darya and Chu-Talas) stays. Repair round: of the +1,925 cells, 729 lie in Kazakhstan (Qyzylorda 407, South Kazakhstan 264, Zhambyl 36, with a few border cells) and are kept as a gain from the Uzbek heirs of Abu'l-Khayr (ledger 1475, confidence 1, from the capital Syghanaq on the middle Syr Darya, the Janibek Khan page and the 1495-1496 division 'several cities of northern Turkestan' retained by the Kazakhs); 1,196 in Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan are removed. The 270 cells shared with the timurid-empire dossier's Transoxiana correction are reported to its owner. [fx-15] The Kyrgyz Fergana valley (Jalal-Abad, 24-27 cells) is also left out: the Umar Shaikh Mirza II page has the Timurid Umar Shaikh Mirza II ruling the Fergana Valley from 8 February 1469 to 10 June 1494, succeeded by his son Babur, and no page opened gives it to the Kazakhs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umar_Shaikh_Mirza_II). The Syr Darya oblasts of Kazakhstan are no longer claimed by the timurid-empire keyframes from 1447 (F085).

1502-1511, 1,738,222 km2. The 431 cells Cliopatria drops (64.4-73.2E, 37.4-42.2N: Samarkand, Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya) all pass to its Shaybanids shape and are the Timurid lands Shaybani took in 1500-1501, not Kazakh land (see 1475). What remains is the steppe, the Chu-Talas valleys and the middle Syr Darya round the capital Syghanaq; Muhammad Shaybani raided northward into Kazakh lands in 1508-09, and Kasym defeated his forces in 1510. Four Tashkent cells (8%) are left in the shape and are immaterial. [fx-15] Without the 4 Tashkent cells Cliopatria's shape still draws Kazakh: the Moghulistan page has Yunus Khan take Tashkent from the Timurids in 1484 (1482 elsewhere on the page), Mahmud Khan (1487-1508) ruling western Moghulistan from Tashkent, and the Uzbeks seizing it after 1503; the Kazakh Khanate page gives the Kazakhs no hold on Tashkent before the struggle of Kasym's last years (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moghulistan).

1521-1528, 2,400,405 km2: Kasym's peak. 'Kazakh authority extended from the territory of present-day southeastern Kazakhstan to the Ural Mountains'; 'the southern borders ... extended to the right bank of the Syr Darya, including Tashkent'; 'in the northwest they reached the Yaik River basin'; Saray-Juk taken in 1520 (708 of the 2,222 new cells come from the Nogai Horde shape, 474 from Western Moghulistan). The page gives no area; it gives the population as 'reached 1 million people'. The shape also holds Kyzylkum and Ustyurt south of the Syr Darya (Navoi 43%, Karakalpakstan 26%), which the page does not claim; with soft steppe borders that stays. Tashkent: the Tashkent page says 'In the 16th century, Tashkent was ruled by the Shaybanid dynasty', which disagrees with the Kazakh page.

unverified: page budget. 1529-1555, 2,400,538 km2, flat on Cliopatria. The page says that after Kasym's death the khanate declined sharply and reports Muhammad Haidar Dughlat's view that after 1533-1534 the Kazakhs were 'completely uprooted'; Haqnazar (1538-1580) regained the eastern Qipchaq Steppe in the 1550s. No land is named, so the 1521 shape stands as a ceiling and the whole span is soft. A gap-filler should read the Haqnazar Khan and Tarikh-i Rashidi pages. Repair round: the Haqnazar Khan page was opened: reign 1538-1580; he 'united the scattered inhabitants of the steppe from the former Kazakh Khanate after the 1520s'; it is silent on 1533-1534 and names no lost land, so the verdict stays ok (soft).

unverified: page budget. 1556-1568, 2,400,625 km2. Haqnazar defeats the Manghits in the 1550s, captures Ismail's relatives in 1557 and wins at the Emba in 1568; the Moghulistan page has Abdurashid fight the 'Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde' for western Moghulistan 1533-1565 and the Kazakh page has Oirat and Moghul forces beat Haqnazar in the 1560s when he tried to take Jetisu, so Semirechye is contested here (ledger 1533-1565) though the shape draws it as Kazakh. Repair round: the Haqnazar Khan page was opened: reign 1538-1580; he 'united the scattered inhabitants of the steppe from the former Kazakh Khanate after the 1520s'; it is silent on 1533-1534 and names no lost land, so the verdict stays ok (soft).

The page has the Kazakhs defeat the Nogai Horde at the Emba River in 1568 and by 1569 the Manghit nomads east of the Ural River absorbed (ledger 1568-1569); the shape is right, the date is three years early on the page. The Haqnazar Khan page (opened in the repair round) says 'In 1570, Haqnazar defeated the Nogai Horde at the Battle of Emba', two years after the Kazakh Khanate page; the shape is right, the 1568-1569 dates are the Kazakh page's.

The 309 cells added (52.1-73.7E, 39.1-53.5N, 304 from Cliopatria's Khanate of Bukhara) are Tawakkul's conquests: the page has him invade in 1597-1598 and capture Tashkent, Turkistan, Andijan and Samarqand but fail to take Bukhara. Cliopatria starts them in 1595; the page dates them 1597-1598 (ledger 1597).

1600-1608, 2,652,434 km2: still holds Tawakkul's Samarkand-Andijan lands. The page is silent on when they were lost; Tawakkul's reign ends in 1598, Esim's begins, and the page has Tashkent, Turkestan and the surrounding districts held by the Kazakh Khanate for about 200 years under a truce with the Astrakhanids. Cliopatria drops the Zarafshan cells in 1609 (ledger 1609, confidence 1); Esim moves the capital from Sygnak to Turkestan (1599 in the infobox).

1609-1635, 2,559,568 km2: the steppe, Semirechye, Tashkent and the Syr Darya. Esim captures Tashkent in 1611 and again in 1613 (so it did not stay Kazakh throughout; ledger 1611-1613) and drives the Karakalpaks off the middle Syr Darya in 1613; in the mid-1610s he takes refuge in Moghulistan. The Tashkent page says 'From 1598 to 1604 Tashkent was ruled by the Shaybanid Keldi Muhammad', which the shape ignores.

keyframe_review.note: 1636-1658, 2,213,712 km2. Cliopatria drops 1,149 cells in 1636 (73.4-85.5E, 42.2-49.2N, 1,067 of them into its Oirat Confederation shape): Semirechye east of the Talas and the land to the upper Irtysh. The Kazakh-Dzungar Wars page dates the first loss of ground later: 'In 1643, an army led by Erdeni Batur invaded Jetisu', the Dzungars later held the eastern Semirechye, and the border was set 'from the Ayagöz River to the Talas River' (the Dzungar Khanate page dates the fixing of the border to 1658). So Jetisu stays Kazakh, contested from 1643, until 1658 (ledger 1643, 1658).

The 41 cells lost (69.9-74.2E, 42.5-44.1N) go to Cliopatria's Dzungar Khanate shape and are Sayram: the page has Sayram captured by Galdan's forces in 1684 (after failed sieges in 1681 and 1683), freed by a revolt of the townspeople and retaken by Galdan; the Kazakh return of 1687 is Cliopatria's (ledger 1684, 1687).

1687-1717, 2,213,712 km2: Sayram back (41 cells from the Dzungar shape, 1687). The page gives the retaking no year; Tauke Khan (1680-1715) retook Jetisu in the succession war and codified the Jeti Zhargy. In 1689 a Kazakh coalition struck the Dzungar rear; in 1698 'a 40,000-strong Dzungar army defeated the Kazakh uluses of the Senior jüz'.

1718-1720, 2,210,720 km2: eleven cells on the Irtysh go to Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia (ledger 1718). The Semey page dates the first Russian settlement there, the Semipalatinsk fort, to 1718, so the year is page-backed; the region is Cliopatria's. Tauke died in 1715 or 1718, after which the zhuzes 'essentially became independent khanates'; the first khans of the three zhuzes were established in 1721 (Juz page).

wars.name: Kazakh-Shaybanid wars of Burunduk and Kasym

zones.text: the Syr Darya lands and the southern cities Otrar, Yasi, Arkuq and Uzgend

union.text: Saray-Juk (Saraishyq), the Nogai capital Kasym captured in 1520

wars.name: Kazakh-Moghul struggle for western Moghulistan
wars.outcome: Abdurashid Khan of the Yarkent Khanate fights the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde for western Moghulistan; it is ultimately lost and the Moghuls are largely restricted to the Tarim Basin; Oirat and Moghul forces beat Haqnazar in Jetisu in the 1560s.

wars.name: Haqnazar's war with the Nogai Horde

zones.text: the steppe between the Emba and the Ural

wars.outcome: The Kazakhs defeat the Nogais at the Emba River in 1568 and reach Astrakhan, where Russian forces repel them; the Manghit nomads east of the Ural are absorbed by 1569.
wars.note: The Haqnazar Khan page (not opened here) dates the Emba battle 1570.

wars.name: Tawakkul Khan's invasion of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Tawakkul captures Tashkent, Turkistan, Andijan and Samarkand but fails to take Bukhara; Tashkent and Turkestan stay Kazakh for about 200 years under a truce with the Astrakhanids.
wars.note: The Tashkent page says the peace of 1598 left Tashkent under Kazakh control and also that the Shaybanid Keldi Muhammad ruled it 1598-1604.

wars.name: Esim Khan's Tashkent campaigns
wars.outcome: Esim captures Tashkent in 1611 and again in 1613 and drives the Karakalpaks out of the middle Syr Darya in 1613.

wars.name: Kazakh-Dzungar Wars

zones.text: Jetisu: invaded 1643, eastern part held by the Dzungars from the 1650s
Tashkent, Turkestan and the Syr Darya cities, taken in 1723
Sayram, taken by Galdan's forces in 1684

wars.outcome: The Dzungars take eastern Semirechye (border 'from the Ayagöz River to the Talas River', 1658), Sayram in 1684 and the southern cities in 1723; they hold Jetisu and Tashkent until 1745, make the jüzes recognise their overlordship in 1740-1742 and lose their power after Galdan Tseren's death in 1745.
wars.note: Phases on the page: 1635-1658; 1681-1698 (Galdan's campaign on Jetisu 1681, the coalition of 1689, defeat of the Senior jüz in 1698); 1710-1716; the 'Barefooted Flight' of 1723; Bulanty and Anrakai 1726-1730; the invasion of the Middle Jüz in late February 1741 and the end of the war in May 1741, hostilities again in 1742. The page is silent on 1755-1758; the Dzungar Khanate page has the final clashes with the Middle Jüz in 1752-1755 and Ablai negotiating with the Qing in summer 1757.

wars.name: Abylai's war with Kokand for Tashkent
wars.outcome: Irdana Biy of Kokand takes Tashkent for a time in 1765 and Ablay Khan retakes it.
wars.note: The Kazakh Khanate page has Abylai 'led numerous campaigns against the Kokand Khanate and the Kyrgyz' and capture Tashkent in his last campaign, with no year.

wars.name: Kenesary Kasymov's revolt

zones.text: the Middle Jüz steppe: Akmolinsk taken in May 1838, Kenesary khan 1841

wars.outcome: Kenesary's revolt against Russian rule and Kokand ends with his death in 1847; the Kazakh Khanate ends with him.
wars.note: The page says the revolt aimed to free the southern Kazakhs from Kokand rule but gives no battles; it says Kenesary was killed fighting Kyrgyz manaps, while the Kazakh Khanate page says Kokand forces.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout: nomad pasture ranges, no treaty lines. The nearest to a fixed line are the Dzungar frontier from the Ayagöz River to the Talas River (1658, a river line) and the Russian forts and lines of the 18th and 19th centuries, which the pages opened do not date; both stay soft. The frontier on the Syr Darya is a river line, softer in the Kyzylkum and Ustyurt to the south.

notes:
Phase B dossier for ia-03-a, written 2026-10-19 from 14 opened Wikipedia pages (the page budget for 43 shapes is 14); one more page, Lesser Juz (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_J%C3%BCz), did not load (url_not_found, retried once) and is not a source. Memory is not used as a source; where a page is silent the event is at confidence 1.

WHAT THE PAGES COULD NOT SETTLE
1. Infobox area: the Kazakh Khanate infobox gives none, so Cliopatria's areas (peak 2.65 M km2 in 1595-1608; 2.40 M in 1521-1571; 1.71 M in 1822-1847) are uncompared; the page gives only a population that 'reached 1 million people' under Kasym.
2. Founding: the page dates the khanate 1465 (Kazakh historiography) or 1470-1471 (Russian); Cliopatria's first shape is 1468; the Kerei page gives no founding year (late 1450s breakaway). The dossier starts in 1465 and adds a new keyframe for 1465-1467.
3. Cliopatria's 1475-1501 shapes contain the Timurid and Shaybanid heartland (Samarkand, Bukhara, Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, Khatlon, Tashkent: 1,925 cells taken from the Timurid shape in 1475). No opened page supports it and two contradict it (Moghulistan: Tashkent taken from the Timurids in 1482 or 1484, lost to Shaybani in 1503; Muhammad Shaybani: Samarkand from the Timurids in 1500). Verdict adjust for 1475-1497 with the 1,196 Uzbek, Tajik and Turkmen cells removed. The 729 cells in Kazakhstan (the middle and lower Syr Darya) are kept and now have a gain event (ledger 1475, confidence 1, counterpart the Uzbek heirs of Abu'l-Khayr): the infobox capital Syghanaq (from 1469), the Janibek Khan page (died c. 1480 at Sighnaq, Kazakh Khanate) and the Kazakh page's 1495-1496 division ('the Kazakh rulers retained control over several cities of northern Turkestan') support a Kazakh hold before 1496, but no page dates its start. 270 of the cells (264 in South Kazakhstan) lie in the timurid-empire dossier's Transoxiana corrections of 1475-1500 and are claimed twice: the ia-02 owner must reconcile (drop them from the Timurid region or date their loss).
4. The Syr Darya in 1510: the Kasym Khan page has the Uzbek Khanate agree to give 'all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya' without a year; Cliopatria adds them in 1521 (956 cells from its Bukhara shape). Dated 1510 at confidence 1; the 1512-1520 shapes are adjusted to include South Kazakhstan and Qyzylorda.
5. Tashkent: the Kazakh page has it Kazakh at Kasym's death, 'between 1598 and 1723' (Tashkent page), and as a second capital 1729-1781, but also Shaybanid in the 16th century, ruled by Keldi Muhammad 1598-1604, under the Dzungars 1723-1745, taken for a time by Irdana Biy of Kokand in 1765, independent under Yunus Khoja 1784-1807 and annexed by Kokand in 1809. All dated in the ledger; Cliopatria keeps the oasis Kazakh to 1809 and the shapes of 1783-1846 are adjusted to remove it from 1784. A 'Tashkent state (Yunus Khoja), 1784-1809' dossier is needed (counterpart in the 1784 loss).
6. Decline after Kasym (c. 1521): the Kazakh page says the khanate declined sharply after Kasym and reports that the Kazakhs were 'completely uprooted' after 1533-1534; Cliopatria keeps the 1521 shape flat to 1571. No land is named, so shapes 1529 and 1556 are ok with 'unverified: page budget' and a contest over Semirechye 1533-1565 is recorded; the Haqnazar Khan page and Muhammad Haidar Dughlat's Tarikh-i Rashidi are the places to look.
7. Russian lines and forts: the Irtysh, Ishim, Orenburg and Siberian lines are not dated on any page opened; Cliopatria's small losses to the Tsardom and the Russian Empire (1718, 1721, 1738, 1769) are confidence 1. Repair round: Orenburg, Semey, Omsk and Ust-Kamenogorsk were opened; only the Semey page (fort 1718) dates a Cliopatria move, the 1718 loss, now confidence 2; the 1721, 1738 and 1769 moves stay Cliopatria's. Not opened: Siberian Line, Russian conquest of Central Asia.
8. The Khiva loss of 1791 (725 cells) and the Kokand losses of 1809 and 1822 (259 and 396 cells) are Cliopatria's; only the Tashkent annexation of 1809 and 'the 1820s' are on pages. Repair round: Khanate of Khiva, Turkistan (city), Taraz and Kyzylorda were opened and date none of these moves; the Kyzylorda page puts a Kokand fortress, Ak-Mechet, at about 1817 on the strip Cliopatria returns to the Kazakhs from Khiva in 1822. Not opened: Senior Juz; the Lesser Jüz page still does not load.
9. The Russian oaths: 10 October 1731 (Junior Juz, Abu'l Khayr to Empress Anna), shortly after by Semeke of the Middle Juz; the Jüz page dates the Middle jüz's incorporation 1734-1740 and the Abylai page his oath at Orenburg 1740; a footnote (Bregel): the oaths were made 'between 1731 and 1740' and stayed purely nominal until the end of the 18th century. These are Russian suzerainty over Kazakh lands: they belong to the Russian Empire dossier (vassal_start, counterpart kazakh-khanate, Junior Juz 1731, Middle Juz 1740) and not to this ledger, which would put the khanate's own vassals. Likewise the Dzungar overlordship of the Greater and Middle Juz (1734-1735 and 1740-1742) and of the Junior Juz (1742) belongs to the Dzungar dossier, and the Qing suzerainty over Abylai (1757) to qing-dynasty.
10. The three jüzes: after Tauke (1715 or 1718) the zhuzes 'essentially became independent khanates' and the first khans of the three zhuzes were established in 1721 (Juz page); Abylai ruled all three from 1771 to 1781, Vali the northern Middle Juz after him. Cliopatria keeps one Kazakh shape; this dossier follows it and records the Russian takeover of the Middle Juz (1822) and Junior Juz (1824) as hatched occupation, ending in 1837 (Kenesary's revolt, contest) and 1847.
11. 1846-1847: the Kenesary page has him killed by Kyrgyz manaps and calls him the last khan; the Kazakh page has him surrender in 1846 and die fighting Kokand forces. The khanate's end year 1847 is Cliopatria's and the infobox's.
12. Rulers: the page's table (copied) has gaps, 1715-1771 and 1781-1841, and overlapping claimants in 1533-1538; Kerei's reign is given as 1456-1473 and 1465-1480 on the same page. The strip is a record, not a succession.
13. Capitals: Sozaq, Syghanaq and Saraishyq are not in the gazetteer; the coordinates are approximate (listed in each capital's note). The infobox capital dates (Turkistan 1599-1781, Tashkent 1729-1781) are taken as given; Saraishyq (infobox 1511-1521) is dated 1520 only, the year the same page has Kasym capture Saray-Juk, and sits in the 1520 contest zone.
14. Counterpart rows: Cliopatria's Oirat Confederation (1619-1676) and Dzungar Khanate (1609-1618, 1677-1756) rows are the Dzungars of the page; 1643 and 1658 use oirat-confederation, 1684 and later dzungar-khanate. Cliopatria's Western Moghulistan is the Semirechye part of Moghulistan.
